item.title: Why Senate Democrats blocked a bill to limit lawmakers' stock trades
item.description: A bill that would have prohibited lawmakers and their family members from buying publicly-traded stocks was blocked by Senate Democrats on Wednesday over an attached rider on voter ID laws. CBS News' Taurean Small reports.

item.title: Middle East oil exports back to 80% of prewar levels, but prices still high
item.description: The Middle East's oil exports have risen to about 80% of prewar levels, according to oil tracker Kpler, but prices have remained high. CBS News' Aaron Maclean has more.

item.title: AI expert skeptical of companies' pledge to implement safety measures
item.description: A White House meeting on AI regulation ended with tech leaders agreeing on an AI "constitution." Stuart Russell, president of the International Association for Safe and Ethical AI, joins "The Daily Report" to break it down.

item.title: GOP Senate candidate Ken Paxton says Trump's midterm convention hurt him in leaked audio
item.description: Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton can be heard in a leaked audio recording observing that President Trump's GOP midterms convention was politically harmful for the GOP. CBS News' Zak Hudak has more.

item.title: District attorney in Cornell case claims he never saw police transcript with alleged rape victim
item.description: The district attorney in the alleged Cornell University rape case says he never saw a transcript of the accuser's conversation with campus police where she said she was raped. CBS News' Anna Schecter has more details.

item.title: Iran says it received U.S. counterproposal to ceasefire plan
item.description: Iran says it has received a U.S. counterproposal to the seven-day ceasefire plan that was rejected by the White House. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi has more.

item.title: Alleged pilot stabbing aboard Israel-bound flight investigated as possible terrorism
item.description: New details are emerging on the stabbing that took place aboard an Israel-bound FlyDubai flight on Wednesday. CBS News' Tina Kraus reports and Neria Kraus, a senior journalist and Middle East analyst who reported on the incident for the Free Press, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss. The Free Press is a Paramount publication.

item.title: Iranian photojournalist facing 15 years in prison speaks out
item.description: Yalda Moaiery, an Iranian photojournalist who has spent her career documenting life in her home country, was sentenced to 15 years in prison in connection with her work. CBS News' Courtney Kealy has the details.

item.title: Cornell Jane Doe told campus police, "I can say with 100% confidence I was raped," transcript shows
item.description: The accuser in the alleged Cornell University gang rape told campus authorities she was "100%" sure she was raped just days after the incident, an interview transcript reviewed by CBS News New York shows. CBS News' Lilia Luciano has more.

item.title: Ethics expert on taxpayers paying for Trump's new ads
item.description: Christopher Swartz, former acting chief of ethics law at the U.S. Office of Government Ethics, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss the controversy over a series of new White House television ads paid for by taxpayers.

item.title: The state of key races 35 days before midterms
item.description: A new poll from Marist shows Democrats leading the Senate and gubernatorial races in Ohio just 35 days before the midterms. CBS News' political director Fin Gómez breaks it down.

item.title: Why Lindsay Clancy's attorney is only now questioning whether she committed killings
item.description: CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson breaks down why Lindsay Clancy's attorney might have decided now to question whether she committed the killings of her three children during a hearing on the timing of a potential new trial.

item.title: Winter holiday flight prices reach 10-year high in U.S. as Iran war sends fuel costs soaring
item.description: Winter holiday airfares reached a 10-year high in the U.S. amid Iran war price hikes, a new analysis by Hopper found. CBS News' Megan Cerullo has more.

item.title: Takeaways from Lindsay Clancy court appearance as lawyer questions if Clancy killed her kids
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's defense attorney cast doubt Tuesday on whether she committed the murders of her three children. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul has new details.

item.title: Trump and tech leaders sign "morally-binding" AI "constitution" in safety push
item.description: President Trump met with key AI leaders at the White House on Tuesday, with the group signing what Mr. Trump called an AI "constitution" aimed at self-policing and safety. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi has more.

item.title: Questions rise after Trump announces $15 billion Iowa steel plant
item.description: President Trump on Monday announced that a prominent steel company would build a $15 billion plant in Iowa. CBS News' Lana Zak reports.

item.title: MLB playoffs to begin with Wild Card round that includes Yankees-Red Sox matchup
item.description: Major League Baseball's grueling 162-game regular season ended on Sunday and postseason baseball is here. Four games kick off the wild-card round starting Tuesday. Levi Weaver, a staff writer for The Athletic, previews the MLB playoffs.

item.title: Russian drone hits cultural landmark in Ukraine's capital
item.description: Russia struck a cultural landmark in Ukraine on Monday, the National Academy of Sciences, killing at least seven people and wounding dozens more. They also attacked apartment buildings, offices and data centers. CBS News international reporter Aidan Stretch was forced to take shelter shortly after creating this report. CBS News national security analyst Aaron MacLean also has more on the war.

item.title: Nvidia announces new software to prevent AI agents from "going rogue"
item.description: Technology company and chip maker Nvidia has created a new security platform aimed at preventing artificial intelligence agents from going rogue. Connor Leahy, executive director of ControlAI, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Fetterman says it's "entirely possible" for Democrats to take back Senate in midterms
item.description: The 2026 midterm elections are a little over a month away and Democrats are hoping to win back both chambers of Congress. CBS News' Taurean Small reports.

item.title: Cleanup underway after powerful nor'easter batters East Coast
item.description: Recovery efforts are underway in parts of the northeaster after a nor'easter brought destructive winds and heavy rain over the weekend. CBS News' Rob Marciano has more.

item.title: What to know as criminal probe reopened into alleged 2024 Cornell gang rape
item.description: Prosecutors say they are reopening an investigation into an alleged 2024 gang rape at Cornell University. CBS News' Anna Schecter reports.

item.title: What to watch for at this weekend's MTV Video Music Awards
item.description: The 2026 MTV Video Music Awards will be held this weekend with Snoop Dogg carrying out hosting duties. "Entertainment Tonight" correspondent Denny Directo joins CBS News for a preview.

item.title: How El Niño is supercharging Pacific storms
item.description: While El Niño is a natural shift in the climate system, scientists say the weather pattern developing in the Pacific Ocean could be one of the strongest on record. And human-caused climate change is super-charging its strength, making weather extremes worse. Tracy Wholf, founder of WereWHOLF Media, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Supreme Court allows use of database to review voter rolls
item.description: The Supreme Court on Friday sided with the Trump administration in its push to use a controversial database to review state voter rolls. David Becker, executive director at the Center for Election Innovation and Research, joins CBS News to discuss what this means for voters.

item.title: What to know about "panda diplomacy" as China sends 2 more furry friends to U.S.
item.description: China says it's sending two pandas to Zoo Atlanta, bringing the total number of Chinese pandas in the U.S. to six. Neil Thomas, senior fellow at the Asia Society's Center for China Analysis, joins CBS News to discuss the ins and outs of panda diplomacy.

item.title: U.S. military laying groundwork for potential action around Cuba
item.description: The U.S. Army Reserve is examining whether it can provide the military's Southern Command with police forces, medical personnel and other support units within the next four months, according to an internal Army message reviewed by CBS News. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: Scant details so far on what came from Trump-Xi meeting
item.description: President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping wrapped their meeting Friday. CBS News' Natalie Brand has more.

item.title: Latest forecast on nor'easter, Hurricane Nolo with millions under threat this weekend
item.description: Millions on opposite ends of the United States are facing severe weather threats this weekend. CBS News' Tom Hanson, Carter Evans and Lonnie Quinn have the details.

item.title: New polling from Maine, Michigan and New Hampshire shows mixed results for Democrats
item.description: New polls from Maine, Michigan, and New Hampshire show Democratic candidates in mixed positions ahead of midterms. CBS News political reporter Zak Hudak breaks it down.
